title: Regression-aware Hosted Surface PRD and 'Cordon Mode' Launch Checklist
creator: Ava Chen
description: This PRD defines a regression-aware behavioral contract for the consolidated hosted inference surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) and prescribes a phased launch that includes a new 'cordon mode' to limit exposure during early rollout. The goal is to enable faster ship velocity while preventing regressions in quality and latency from reaching broad production traffic.
problem_statement: Prior launches risked surfaced regressions from model updates, batching/quantization changes, or routing policies. We need an explicit behavioral contract and automated gating that detects and contains regressions (quality, latency, and cost) before global rollout.
goals: Provide a single PRD that specifies behavioral contracts across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints
Introduce 'cordon mode' — a deployment lane that serves only low-risk customers and synthetic traffic until regressions pass gating criteria
Define automated acceptance checks (eval suites + telemetry thresholds) that must pass for canary and global phases
Ensure rollback conditions and automatic fallback mapping to stable model variants are in place
non_goals: This PRD does not redesign client SDK surface or billing primitives
It does not change Dedicated capacity autoscaling policies
It does not include on-prem installation procedures beyond compatibility verification
solution_overview: A behavioral contract layer sits above model variants and routing logic. Each endpoint exposes a contract (latency P95, quality delta vs baseline on canonical eval sets, token-cost delta). New releases must run the eval pipeline and live telemetry checks. If any metric crosses a regression threshold, requests are routed into cordon mode or to a stable fallback variant. Deployment phases: dev -> staging -> cordon -> canary -> ramp -> global.
api_contracts: Chat/Completions: must preserve response shape, streaming behavior, and function-call semantics. Latency P95 <= baseline + 30ms for the same profile.
Embeddings: cosine similarity drift vs baseline <= 0.02 on canonical embedding pairs (eval suite).
Rerank: NDCG@10 delta vs baseline >= -0.03 on benchmark datasets.
All endpoints: per-request token-cost increase <= 10% compared to pinned baseline variant or must be explicitly approved by PM.
backward_compatibility: Backward compatibility is required for public API fields and function-calling behavior. Minor internal response ordering differences are allowed if documented and covered by tests. Any breaking change requires a separate deprecation and migration plan.
acceptance_criteria: PRD reviewed and approved by Product, Engineering, and Design leads
End-to-end automated eval pipeline runs successfully for new model variants with documented baselines
Telemetry dashboards showing latency, error-rate, and quality deltas are in place and accessible to oncall
Cordon mode routing exists and can be toggled via config with a runtime flag
Canary traffic decision automation exists: if quality regressions > threshold OR latency SLO violated for 10 minutes, traffic falls back to stable variant
A smoke test matrix covering chat, completions, embeddings, rerank is green in staging
Runbook and rollback playbook published and linked in this ticket
Legal and security signoff for hosted-2025.03 obtained
scope_changes: Scope reduced: initial launch will support only text-based chat/completions + standard embeddings + basic rerank API. Multimodal payloads deferred to a follow-up project.
Added: cordon-mode networking rule to restrict early release to whitelisted orgs and synthetic traffic
Deferred: per-tenant customizable rolling-window evals (will be tracked as PM-330112)
rollout_checklist: Pre-launch: finalize baseline artifacts and pin baseline model variants
Pre-launch: run full eval suite and store results in canonical storage with immutable ID
Staging: execute smoke tests and latency profiles under controlled QPS
Cordon: enable cordon mode and route 2% synthetic + 5 low-risk customers; monitor 24h
Canary: expand to 10% real traffic from diverse regions for 6h while running evals every 30m
Ramp: increase traffic 25% -> 50% over 24h windows if no regression flags
Global: proceed to 100% with monitoring thresholds relaxed to steady-state alerts
Post-launch: 7-day quality sweep and token-cost reconciliation with finance
telemetry_and_observability: Dashboards: per-endpoint P50/P95 latencies, error rates, token-cost per request, model-variant distribution
Quality monitors: daily eval report with delta vs baseline for canonical prompt set
Regression alerts: automated alert if quality delta > configured threshold or latency SLO breached for >10m
Tracing: end-to-end traces with route and model-variant tags for sample failures
Audit logs: record cordon toggles, fallback triggers, and model-variant pins
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: false-positive regressions block releases. Mitigation: require multi-signal agreement (eval + live telemetry + manual triage) before automatic rollback.
Risk: cordon mode prevents necessary load testing. Mitigation: include synthetic QPS generators in cordon and staging.
Risk: increased token-cost surprises customers. Mitigation: pre-announce cost delta to impacted orgs and add cost guardrails in routing rules.
dependencies: ENG-42700: automated eval pipeline (canonical datasets and runner)
ENG-43500: telemetry dashboards and alerting integrations
PM-330112: per-tenant evals (deferred, depends on this launch)
